subject: Computer Networking
title: Signal and Privacy-First Design
description: A micro-lesson that makes Signal and Privacy-First Design usable.

hook.text: Signal collects almost nothing about you. It's the gold standard for private messaging.

buildup.text: Signal Protocol uses double-ratchet encryption. Keys rotate with every message for forward secrecy.

discovery.text: Signal stores only your phone number and last connection date. No message content, no contacts, no metadata.

twist.text: When subpoenaed, Signal can only hand over two data points: the phone number and last connection timestamp.

climax.text: Sealed sender hides who sent a message even from Signal's servers. Metadata protection taken to the extreme.

punchline.text: Signal proves privacy and usability can coexist. No compromise.

quiz.question: What does Signal's double-ratchet encryption provide?
options: Forward secrecy by rotating keys with every message
Faster message delivery than other apps

details.summary: Signal is an open-source messaging app designed from the ground up for privacy. It uses end-to-end encryption for all messages, collects minimal metadata, and its protocol has become the gold standard adopted by WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and Google Messages.
details.whyItMatters: Signal established the encryption standard that now protects billions of messages daily. Its open-source protocol became the foundation for secure messaging across the industry.
takeaways: Signal's protocol is the industry standard for encrypted messaging
It collects minimal metadata beyond phone number registration
WhatsApp, Messenger, and Google Messages use Signal's protocol

faq.question: What makes Signal more private than WhatsApp?
faq.answer: Both use the same encryption protocol, but Signal collects far less metadata. Signal does not store who you contact, when, or how often. WhatsApp collects extensive metadata and shares it with Meta. Signal's open-source code can be audited; WhatsApp's implementation cannot.

faq.question: Why did other companies adopt Signal's protocol?
faq.answer: Signal's protocol was rigorously reviewed by cryptographers and proven secure. It handles key exchange, forward secrecy, and multi-device support elegantly. Building a new encryption protocol is risky. Adopting a proven, audited protocol is faster and more trustworthy.
